culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.name: Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres
culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.teaser: A red theatre topped with giant eggs, packed with Dalí's jokes, and his grave beneath the stage
culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.story: Dalí was born in Figueres on 11 May 1904, and late in life he turned the ruined shell of the town's old theatre into his own monument. The walls are studded with golden bread loaves, the roof carries a row of giant eggs, and inside the rooms run from paintings to stage tricks: a whole room that resolves into the face of the actress Mae West when seen from the right spot, and a car in the courtyard where it rains inside, on the passengers. His tomb lies beneath the building, the slab carved with the noble rank he took from Púbol.
culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.why: Find the viewing point in the Mae West room and wait: the furniture stops being furniture.
facts: Plaça Gala i Salvador Dalí, in the centre of Figueres

culture:Casa-Museu Dalí, Portlligat.name: Casa-Museu Dalí, Portlligat
culture:Casa-Museu Dalí, Portlligat.teaser: The fishermen's huts Dalí bought one by one and joined into the house he worked in for half a century
culture:Casa-Museu Dalí, Portlligat.story: The painter's first purchase on the little bay of Portlligat, in 1930, was one fishermen's hut. Over five decades he and Gala added the neighbouring huts one at a time, each knocked through, until the house stepped up the slope as a chain of white cells, crooked stairways and windows facing the boats. Dalí painted here until Gala's death in 1982. Visits go in small timed groups, which keeps the studio quiet. The sister Cadaqués guide has the full card; from the Costa Brava coves it is a day trip, best paired with the cape.
culture:Casa-Museu Dalí, Portlligat.why: Book first and build the day around the slot: it is the one Dalí stop that cannot be done on a whim.

culture:Castell Gala Dalí, Púbol.name: Castell Gala Dalí, Púbol
culture:Castell Gala Dalí, Púbol.teaser: A ruined castle turned into Gala's private court, which her husband entered by written invitation only
culture:Castell Gala Dalí, Púbol.story: The castle at Púbol was a medieval ruin, inland among the Baix Empordà fields, when Dalí bought it in 1969 as a present for Gala. As he later told the story, she accepted on one condition: he would come only with a letter from her asking him. The garden filled with his spindly-legged elephants while she kept the rooms as her own. After her death in 1982 she was laid in the crypt beneath, and the widower moved in; a bedroom fire in 1984 drove him back to Figueres. Of the three Dalí houses it is the quietest, with gravel paths and thick stone walls.
culture:Castell Gala Dalí, Púbol.why: Go down to the crypt he designed for her: after the Figueres crowds, the silence there is the point.
facts: Púbol, in the municipality of La Pera, between Girona and La Bisbal d'Empordà

culture:Empúries.name: Ruïnes d'Empúries
culture:Empúries.teaser: A Greek trading town and a Roman city side by side, their streets running down to the sand
culture:Empúries.story: Around 575 BCE Greeks from Massalia landed on this shore and called their trading post Emporion, the market. They first settled the islet that is now the village of Sant Martí d'Empúries, the Palaiapolis, then built the Neapolis on the mainland. In 218 BCE Roman legions landed on this beach to cut off Hannibal, and the conquest of Hispania started there; a Roman town later rose on the slope above. No other site in Spain shows a Greek and a Roman city together. Paths thread between foundations, cisterns and mosaic floors under umbrella pines, and the waves break almost at the edge of the excavations.
culture:Empúries.why: Walk up to the Roman forum and look back: the Greek town, the beach and the gulf line up below you.
facts: Just north of L'Escala, on the shore of the Gulf of Roses; a seafront path links it to the town

culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.name: Sant Pere de Rodes
culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.teaser: A Romanesque abbey on the Verdera ridge, with the whole Gulf of Roses spread out below its walls
culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.story: Recorded from 878, this Benedictine house clings to the flank of the Verdera ridge over El Port de la Selva, and for centuries it was one of the great landholders of the Empordà, its estates keeping vineyards worked through the Middle Ages. Its church justifies the drive up: soaring columns, capitals cut with leaves and beasts, a nave too vast for a mountain ledge, with the cloister and bell tower beside it. From the forecourt the coast unrolls north and east to Cap de Creus. Out of season, with the tramuntana up, you may share it with almost no one.
culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.why: Stay on the forecourt until the office closes: the late light along the cape is the reward for the climb.

culture:Santa Maria, Castelló d'Empúries.name: Santa Maria, Castelló d'Empúries
culture:Santa Maria, Castelló d'Empúries.teaser: A church the size of a cathedral in a town of narrow lanes: the old seat of the Counts of Empúries
culture:Santa Maria, Castelló d'Empúries.story: In the eleventh century the Counts of Empúries moved their capital inland to Castelló, and its church of Santa Maria, consecrated in 1064, grew with them. Rebuilt in Gothic style from the late thirteenth century, it has the plan and size of a cathedral, which is why people here call it the Cathedral of l'Empordà; the Romanesque bell tower survives almost intact from the first church. Behind the altar stands an alabaster retable, described as the last Gothic stone altarpiece in Catalonia, and left unfinished: eight of its niches were never carved. Most cars pass it on the way to the beaches.
culture:Santa Maria, Castelló d'Empúries.why: Stand close to the alabaster retable and find the empty niches: the plan outran the money or the time.
facts: The old town of Castelló d'Empúries, between Figueres and Roses

culture:Cap de Creus.name: Parc Natural de Cap de Creus
culture:Cap de Creus.teaser: Where the Pyrenees run into the sea: bare rock, salt wind and Iberia's easternmost point
culture:Cap de Creus.story: The last spur of the Pyrenees ends here in a natural park of land and sea, a peninsula of bare, folded rock with almost no trees, scoured by the tramuntana and the salt. A single road wriggles out from Cadaqués to the lighthouse on Iberia's most easterly headland, where the former keepers' houses hold the park's small interpretation centre. On the north side the Paratge de Tudela is a field of rock worn into shapes that look like animals and faces. Autumn gusts can be dangerous on the headland. The Cadaqués guide covers the lighthouse in detail.
culture:Cap de Creus.why: Walk the Paratge de Tudela path on a calm day: the rock does stranger things than any painting of it.
facts: The peninsula north and east of Cadaqués; the lighthouse is at the end of the road east of town

culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi.name: elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi
culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi.teaser: The old elBulli above Cala Montjoi, now rooms that show how a team invented 1,846 dishes
culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi.story: On 15 June 2023 the house above Cala Montjoi reopened as elBulli1846, an archive you can walk through, whose number counts the dishes its team created. A headphone guide takes you through the former kitchen and dining room, then some 69 installations over about 4,000 m² that trace how an idea turned into a plate, and finally down to the cove, part of the natural park. Its gates closed for 2026 on 12 October and stay shut until the 2027 season; for the restaurant's history, see the food-history fold.
culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi.why: Linger in the old kitchen: it is smaller than you expect, and that is the lesson.

craft:Do this one.name: Annick Galimont's workshop, La Bisbal d'Empordà
craft:Do this one.teaser: Shape your own cup or bowl at a working ceramist's bench in La Bisbal, inland from the Palafrugell coves
craft:Do this one.story: Clay is what La Bisbal d'Empordà lives on: shop after ceramics shop lines its long main street, and since 2016 the local school has trained young potters, who are opening workshops of their own. Annick Galimont makes soft, pastel tableware in a small workshop-shop on l'Aigüeta, and for years has let visitors sit at her bench to shape a piece instead of buying one. Sessions take two to five people, in English, French, Catalan or Spanish, and the piece goes home with you. Nowhere else on this coast did we find a named maker who will teach.
craft:Do this one.why: Book a two-hour session: one hour is enough to touch the clay, two to make something you will keep.
facts: Shape a piece of ceramics at the bench with the ceramist, in a group of two to five

craft:Other one.name: Museu del Suro de Catalunya, Palafrugell
craft:Other one.teaser: From cork oak to wine stopper: the Gavarres cork craft, told in Palafrugell's museum
craft:Other one.story: Behind the Palafrugell coves rise the cork oaks of the Gavarres, and for generations this town lived on turning their bark into wine stoppers. The Museu del Suro de Catalunya keeps that trade: the tools, the machines and the long road from tree to tap. In early summer it takes the craft outdoors, with demonstrations of the pela, the stripping of bark from living trees, in the woods and in town squares, paired with Empordà wine tastings. It is the best place on the coast to understand cork. Missing: a stopper-maker; no named artisan teaches the cutting, and the hands-on sessions are demonstrations, not lessons.
craft:Other one.why: Come for the summer bark-stripping demonstrations; then every cork you pull in the Empordà means more.
facts: Visit the museum; in early summer, watch cork stripped from the trees and taste Empordà wine

craft:Other two.name: The wooden boats of Palamós
craft:Other two.teaser: The llagut and the mestre d'aixa: a boat-building craft you can still see, but not yet learn
craft:Other two.story: For centuries the boats of this coast were built in wood on the beach by the mestres d'aixa, the shipwrights, and caulked by the calafats. Fibreglass ended that from the 1980s: an ethnological study of the Costa Brava's shipwrights found that the last wooden fishing boat registered in Palamós dates from 1989, and that none of the coast's registered fishing boats is now wooden. The old craft survives in restored llaguts at regattas and in harbour museums, and in a few yards, such as Quico Despuig's in Cadaqués until recently. Missing: a yard that teaches; we found no Costa Brava course open to visitors.
craft:Other two.why: Look at the hulls drawn up at Calella's Port Bo and Palamós: the curve of a wooden llagut is the craft itself.
facts: See the fishing fleet and its history at the Museu de la Pesca in Palamós (its own card, with the Espai del Peix); no hands-on course found

craft:What is sold as local craft.name: What is sold as local craft
craft:What is sold as local craft.teaser: A glazed bowl on a beachfront shelf is not La Bisbal pottery until the base says so
craft:What is sold as local craft.story: The souvenir streets of the big resorts, Lloret's front above all, sell the Costa Brava back to its visitors: melting-clock magnets, Dalí moustache mugs, painted bowls labelled Catalan or Mediterranean, and straw bags beside them. A Dalí souvenir is merchandise of a painter, not something made here, and few shops pretend otherwise. The trouble is the vaguer word, handmade, on pottery that names no town and no maker. No published report names a shop here, so read this as advice on reading labels, not a charge against anyone. La Bisbal, inland, is where Empordà clay is actually worked and fired.
craft:What is sold as local craft.why: Buy pottery where the kiln is: in La Bisbal the person selling it often made it.
facts: Turn the piece over: a maker's mark and a town are good signs; a sticker naming only a country, or nothing, is not local work
Pottery from a La Bisbal workshop; for cork, the Museu del Suro in Palafrugell rather than a resort shelf; anchovies and Empordà wine, which have their own cards
